missionPremise: Twice-confirmed defect per the dispatch: an external Cloud Run cancel never reaches writeTermination in the shared Factory job-runner, leaving run rows stuck at status='running' forever (122cd0b2, the b-gate-sched instance). Root cause named in the dispatch: no SIGTERM handler in the shared runner pattern. Confirmed live before writing any code: grepped every src/jobs/*.mjs for process.on/process.once SIGTERM/SIGINT -- only conformant.mjs and restamp-access.mjs (2 of ~20 job files) ever wired one, each ad hoc and job-local, not shared.

rootCauseVerification.grep: grep -rn "process.on|SIGTERM|SIGINT" src/ --include=*.mjs (excluding test/) returned exactly two hits, both job-local closures capturing their own runId/lease.
rootCauseVerification.everyJobCallsStartRun: grep -c 'await startRun(' across src/jobs/*.mjs: 26 call sites across 24 files (reap.mjs 3, f10-cad-loop.mjs 2, all others 1) -- confirms startRun is the one universal choke point every job already passes through, making it the correct place to hook a guard that cannot be forgotten.

designChoice: Hooked the guard into startRun (src/control/runs.mjs) itself rather than requiring each job to opt in: every startRun caller already exists, so every job inherits the guard for free and a future job cannot forget to wire it. Tracks every run this process has opened in a module-level Map (never deregistered on normal completion -- writeTermination's own ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a retried write on an already-terminated run a harmless no-op, so correctness does not depend on precise bookkeeping of when a run finished). On SIGTERM/SIGINT, best-effort writeTermination(exit_kind:'killed', recorder:'sigterm-guard', reason:'external <signal>') for each still-open run, then process.exit with the conventional code for the signal received (143/130).

testPlan.unitFalsifier: test/sigterm-guard.test.mjs, 5 tests: SIGTERM writes a killed record for a tracked run; SIGINT exits 130; a race against the job's own normal-path termination write is a harmless no-op (no crash, no duplicate event); and the falsifier -- same installed listener, same writeTermination machinery, the ONLY variable is whether the run is still tracked at signal time. Tracked: 1 termination write. Untracked (the pre-fix shape): 0 termination writes. Proves the tracking, not mere listener presence, is the causal mechanism.
